item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is closer to the frozen contract: Files.Upload validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile, and delegates directly to FilesService.Add. B materially changes Add and bypasses it from Upload.","reasons":["A preserves FilesService.Add unchanged and routes Upload through it, retaining existing option handling, request construction, decoding, and error semantics.","A uses the required multipartbody.NewFile helper with field name \"file\" and propagates helper/source-reader errors.","B eagerly reads and buffers every Add body, changing the preserved lower-level API’s consumption timing, memory behavior, and read-error wrapping.","B's Upload calls a new private add method instead of the contractually required existing Add method, duplicating the request path split the contract sought to avoid semantics drifting across routes."],"risks_a":["It adds unrelated PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the specified convenience API.","Upload tests do not assert multipart file content and omit explicit validation and source-reader-error cases required by the contract.","The combined validation error is less precise than separate filename and content errors, though both invalid inputs are rejected before a request."],"risks_b":["It violates preservation of FilesService.Add behavior by buffering all custom multipart bodies and changing source-reader error semantics.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, contrary to the explicit routing requirement.","No visible explicit empty-filename or nil-content validation exists in Upload; behavior is delegated implicitly to the helper, and there are no validation or source-reader-error tests."]}
